s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity swelling and pain
salient_findings: Gradually progressive swelling, pain, and stiffness in the left lower leg
Tender, swollen, warm, and erythematous left lower leg
Extensive deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasonography
key_facts: No fever, chest pain, shortness of breath, hemoptysis, or syncope
Medical history of three prior abortions
Recurrent microcytic anemia treated with iron supplementation
Two prior dilation and curettage procedures
No family history of thromboembolic disease
Bilateral dorsalis pedis pulses were palpable
Sensation was intact without ischemic changes
Hemoglobin 9.5 g/dL with an MCV of 63 fL

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity swelling and pain
salient_findings: Gradually progressive swelling, pain, and stiffness in the left lower leg
Tender, swollen, warm, and erythematous left lower leg
Extensive deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasonography
key_facts: No fever, chest pain, shortness of breath, hemoptysis, or syncope
Medical history of three prior abortions
Recurrent microcytic anemia treated with iron supplementation
Two prior dilation and curettage procedures
No family history of thromboembolic disease
Bilateral dorsalis pedis pulses were palpable
Sensation was intact without ischemic changes

shortlist.label: Deep vein thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by Doppler ultrasonography and CT scan

shortlist.label: May-Thurner syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery

shortlist.label: Post-thrombotic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible complication of deep vein thrombosis

shortlist.label: Thrombophlebitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation of the vein with blood clot, consistent with patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Phlegmasia cerulea dolens
shortlist.why_kept: Severe form of deep vein thrombosis, possible given patient's severe symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of extensive deep vein thrombosis in the left lower extremity, combined with the CT scan findings of compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery, is consistent with May-Thurner syndrome, a condition where the left common iliac vein is compressed by the right common iliac artery, leading to thrombosis.

rejected.label: Deep vein thrombosis
rejected.why: While the patient does have deep vein thrombosis, this diagnosis alone does not explain the underlying cause of the thrombosis, which is suggested to be May-Thurner syndrome by the imaging findings.

rejected.label: Post-thrombotic syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically occurs after a DVT has resolved, and is characterized by chronic symptoms such as pain, swelling, and skin changes, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Thrombophlebitis
rejected.why: This condition refers to inflammation of the veins due to a blood clot, but the patient's presentation and imaging findings suggest a more specific diagnosis of May-Thurner syndrome.

rejected.label: Phlegmasia cerulea dolens
rejected.why: This is a severe form of DVT that causes ischemia and gangrene, but the patient's symptoms and examination findings do not suggest ischemic changes or gangrene.
